maya: Heads-up — we're planning a small telemetry header change in the next SDK release that would add routing/quota metadata to requests. want opinions on consent + rollout.
sam: what exactly would the header contain? sample?
neel: +1 needs a sample. also privacy/PII implications.
maya: example:

ci-bot: ```\nx-rw-routing: route=dedicated;policy=latency;quota_bucket=high\nx-rw-sdk-telemetry: sdk=python;version=1.14.0;opt_in=true\n```

maya: intention is to let console show per-route cost & latency breakdowns without reconstructing routing from traces. also helps Optimize suggestions.
olivia: ok but we must make opt-in default false for EU customers atm. consent/legal will push for explicit opt-in.
sam: breaking concern: TS/Go SDKs default flags differ today. if python flips to true by default that fragments telemetry across SDKs.
neel: proposal: default opt_in=false in SDKs; provide `enable_routing_telemetry=True` explicit flag. then roll out usage in console behind a feature flag + section that explains the data stored.
maya: timeline? we need this for the quotas dashboard beta next month.
sam: canary plan: ship SDK change in non-breaking patch that adds header when flag is set. enable console feature flag internally for 10% of orgs, check cost dashboards + user complaints for 2 weeks, then widen.
olivia: also add sampling param? maybe only send header for 1/10 requests to limit cost/ingest.
neel: sampling helps, but will skew per-route counts. we can pair with server-side inference to fill gaps.
maya: question: should we include quota_bucket in header or let server infer? including it simplifies console but is more sensitive.
olivia: prefer server inference. header should be minimal: route id + sdk metadata. quota_bucket inference server-side using policy mapping.
sam: SDK change snippet (python):

ci-bot: ```python\nclient = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., enable_routing_telemetry=True, routing_telemetry_sampling=0.1)\n```

sam: that API is non-breaking if default false. we should mirror same options in TS/Go so docs are consistent.
maya: docs + changelog entry needed. also add migration section: if you relied on per-token routing tags in previous internal beta, you'll need to opt-in.
neel: ops checklist: add telemetry retention note, ensure we don't log any user prompt content in these headers, run a privacy audit.
maya: agreed. I'll open a console FF and post rollouts doc. @sam can you draft SDK PRs for py/ts/go with matching flags and sampling?
sam: will do. target branch today, PRs by EOD. :thumbsup:
olivia: I'll loop in legal on opt-in wording and get us a short consent blurb.
ci-bot: deploy-preview: SDK flag doc created at https://handbook.internal/rw/sdk-telemetry-optin-1795551234 (preview)
maya: thanks — will post follow-up with canary cohort and dashboards to watch. :eyes:
